title: Toilet Refill-Cycle Leak Fingerprint
dataSources: Whole-home water flow (`watermeter:flow`), water pressure (`waterpressure:reading`), irrigation control (`irrigation:zone`), water-heater events (`waterheater:event`), greywater tanks (`greywater:tank`), and utility sensors for pumps and softeners (`sumppump:event`, `wellpump:event`, `watersoftener:status`).
app: Water and plumbing telemetry from smart water meters, pressure sensors, irrigation controllers, sump and well pumps, greywater tanks, and water-heater sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and vendor APIs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=watermeter:flow fixture="toilet"
| bin _time span=30m
| stats count as refill_events avg(flow_liters) as avg_cycle_liters by bathroom _time
| where refill_events>3
description: Looks for unusually frequent refill cycles from the same toilet, a classic sign of a flapper or valve leak.
value: Toilet leaks are easy to miss but costly over time, and repeated refill fingerprints are often the earliest practical signal.
implementation: Tag fixture-level water events from an instrumented toilet or a smart meter classifier and review short repeat cycles.
visualization: Timeline of refill-event counts by bathroom.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Water, Plumbing & Utilities — typical feeds: Whole-home water flow (`watermeter:flow`), sump pump (`sumppump:event`), well pump (`wellpump:event`), pool/spa chemistry (`pool:chemistry`), water softener (`watersoftener:status`), irrigation zones .
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `watermeter:flow`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=watermeter:flow`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Smart water meters (Flume/Flo/HomeWizard), sump- and well-pump sensors, pool/spa controllers, water-softener and irrigation controllers via vendor APIs, MQTT, and HEC..

**Author notes:** Tag fixture-level water events from an instrumented toilet or a smart meter classifier and review short repeat cycles.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "watermeter:flow", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=watermeter:flow earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Toilet Refill-Cycle Leak Fingerprint** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=watermeter:flow`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `refill_events` (> 3) after avg — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `bathroom`, `refill_events`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=watermeter:flow fixture="toilet"
| bin _time span=30m
| stats count as refill_events avg(flow_liters) as avg_cycle_liters by bathroom _time
| where refill_events>3
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=watermeter:flow earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, bathroom, refill_events
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=watermeter:flow earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `refill_events` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=watermeter:flow earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(refill_events) AS p50 perc90(refill_events) AS p90 perc99(refill_events) AS p99 max(refill_events) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.19.12: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Timeline Of Refill-Event Counts By Bathroom (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `watermeter:flow` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=watermeter:flow | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=30m` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `30m` buckets.
